reasoning: The image shows a stem tissue segment covered with and surrounded by abundant pure-white, fluffy/cottony mycelium spreading outward in a fan pattern onto the surrounding surface. This is the classic presentation of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (white mold/timber rot), which produces dense white cottony mycelium on infected stems. The color (pure white, not gray or dark), texture (cottony/fluffy), and spreading pattern are all characteristic of Sclerotinia and distinguish it from Gray Mold, Southern Blight, Rhizopus, and Powdery Mildew.
